classification.difficultyReason: Identify two right-triangle tangent ratios and apply the tangent difference identity.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle ABC with D on AB, segment CD, a right-angle square at B and theta between CA and CD. Coordinate proportions follow the numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: AD=4, DB=1, BC=3; A,D,B are collinear and BC is perpendicular to AB; theta=angle ACD.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied point names, lengths, right-angle mark and theta are visible.

answer.worked:
$\theta=\angle ACB-\angle DCB$. Since $AB=4+1=5$, $\tan\angle ACB=\dfrac{5}{3}$ and $\tan\angle DCB=\dfrac{1}{3}$.

$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{\tan\angle ACB-\tan\angle DCB}{1+\tan\angle ACB\tan\angle DCB}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{\frac{5}{3}-\frac{1}{3}}{1+\frac{5}{3}\times\frac{1}{3}}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{\frac{4}{3}}{\frac{14}{9}}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{6}{7}.\end{align*}$$
